title: NetOps Console — Ping Tool
objective: The diagnostics page lets staff check that a host is reachable. A configuration file on the same machine holds an API token — read it through the tool.

verifier.condition: The tool's command output contains the API token from the configuration file, which the ping command can never print.

weakness: User input is concatenated into a command line that is handed to a shell interpreter, so shell metacharacters let the user run additional commands.
seededData: A SIMULATED shell over an in-memory virtual filesystem (config.ini with a per-instance token, README, motd). No real shell or host file is ever involved.
hints: Think about what the application must do to turn your input into something that runs. How might it assemble the command?
A shell can run more than one command on a line. How do you tell it where one ends?
The interesting file lives near the tool's own directory.
burpNotes: This lab runs a simulated command interpreter over a virtual filesystem — it is safe by construction and never executes anything on the host. Normal input is a hostname; try varying it and read the output carefully.
